arguments.text: Fixed. In `src/click/core.py`, `Option.__init__` gave every flag a `False` default when no default was supplied (`if is_flag and default_is_missing: self.default = False`), so a flag declared `required=True` always had a value and `MissingParameter` was never raised. The condition now reads `if is_flag and default_is_missing and not self.required:`, so required flags have no implicit default and `cli` with no args exits 2 with "Error: Missing option '--flag'." while `--flag` still yields True. Full suite: 488 passed, 21 skipped, 1 xfailed (same as before the change).

arguments.text: `click.termui.prompt` raises `click.exceptions.Abort` (a subclass of `RuntimeError`). Its inner `prompt_func` wraps the actual read in `try/except (KeyboardInterrupt, EOFError)` and re-raises `Abort()`; when `hide_input` is set it also writes a newline first, since getpass doesn't emit one on ^C. The same `Abort` is raised by `confirm` (termui.py:236) and `pause` (termui.py:803) on Ctrl+C/EOF, and `prompt`'s confirmation step re-raises `Abort` if the two entries don't match. The docstring states this: "If the user aborts the input by sending a interrupt signal, this function will catch it and raise a :exc:`Abort` exception."

arguments.text: `fs_enc` is set to the string `"ascii"`. In `_verify_python_env`, the `try` block does `fs_enc = codecs.lookup(getpreferredencoding()).name`; if that raises any `Exception` (e.g. a broken/unknown locale encoding), the `except Exception:` branch falls back to `fs_enc = "ascii"`. Since `"ascii"` is exactly the value the rest of the function treats as "bad environment", that fallback makes click print the "configured to use ASCII as encoding" abort message (plus the POSIX locale hints) and exit.
